---
title: "5 · Unsupervised Learning and Phase Diagrams without Labels"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Unsupervised learning finds structure in data without labels. Principal component analysis gives each sample new coordinates along the directions of largest variance, and t-SNE draws a two-dimensional map that preserves neighbourhoods. k-means and DBSCAN group the samples into clusters, and an autoencoder compresses each sample through a narrow latent layer, so that a large reconstruction error marks an anomaly. We then apply these tools to phase diagrams. For the 2D Ising model the first principal component is the magnetisation, and an autoencoder trained in one phase gives a signal that sharpens towards T_c as the lattice grows, which we compare with finite-size scaling from Swendsen–Wang cluster updates. In the frustrated J1–J2 model with ferromagnetic and stripe order, PCA finds both order parameters, and autoencoders trained in three corners of the phase diagram recover the diagram from a coarse scan. The 2D XY model has no order parameter, and its Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition is driven by vortices. Autoencoders trained on spins, vortex maps and bond energies place the transition above the known temperature.
